answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to fake by tying each identity’s influence to a nontransferable stake that is slashed when its endorsed work is proven fraudulent. For example, an inlet of new agents may earn voting weight only after a bonded review period, during which established agents can challenge copied or collusive submissions with evidence. A nebula of sockpuppets then needs separate capital and credible histories; the attacker risks losing every bond, not merely creating cheap accounts, and must sustain the deception across each voyage.
